producer.summary: High West producer tasting sheet, relayed by a distributor: straight bourbon blend finished in Barbados rum barrels. A sweet fruit and coconut profile with molasses and baking spice.
producer.nose: Coconut, banana bread and custard with darker sugar beneath.
producer.palate: Pastry-like peach, caramel and ginger sweetness.
producer.finish: Soft peach and dark sugar with a tobacco-paper accent.

facts.age: Base blend: 4–9 years in the cited release
facts.cask: Barbados rum barrels; 10 months in cited release
facts.region: Blended and finished in Utah; base distillers not established

critics.nose: Roasted nuts and sweet baking spice.
critics.palate: Vanilla and maple with a root-beer note.
critics.summary: Retailer describes its own selection; used as supporting tasting context, not proof of the pictured batch.

notes: Photo 2 confirms the finish; blend ages and finishing time describe the cited release, not a verified batch in the photo.

producer.summary: NuLu describes its French Oak release as straight bourbon finished with toasted French oak staves. The finish adds toasted-wood character; single barrel releases can differ.

facts.cask: French oak finish; stave/barrel method varies by release
facts.region: NuLu / PCS Distilling, Louisville; base distiller not verified for pictured bottle

critics.nose: Maple and toasted wood with a little cherry.
critics.palate: Rich sweetness with chocolate and oak.
critics.summary: These notes are from the C289 French oak barrel selection; the photo does not establish that selection.

notes: French Oak wording is supported by the photo’s sign. Exact barrel, finishing method, proof and age remain unconfirmed; supporting retailer notes are not an exact-batch review.

producer.summary: Amburana finishing makes this a strongly aromatic bourbon with dessert-like spice. NuLu describes the wood as contributing vanilla, cacao, cinnamon icing, ginger and burnt sugar.

facts.region: NuLu / PCS Distilling, Louisville; base distiller depends on release

critics.nose: Cookie-like cinnamon and vanilla over sweet wood.
critics.palate: Sweet cinnamon with a little dried fruit and citrus.
critics.finish: Spiced cake and sugared fruit; less lingering than expected.
critics.summary: The reviewer found the finish enjoyable but dominant enough to obscure much of the base bourbon. The sampled barrel was not established in the photo.

notes: Proof, age, mash bill and the reviewer’s numeric score are deliberately unset: the photographed batch is unknown. Amburana is commonly called Brazilian oak but is not botanically oak.

producer.summary: The wheated Holladay recipe bottled at Rickhouse Proof rather than diluted to the bonded release’s strength. Proof depends on the batch; the producer combines barrels at their natural strength.

facts.age: At least 6 years; exact batch age unconfirmed

critics.nose: Fruit and caramel with charred wood.
critics.palate: Dark fruit, molasses and leathery oak.
critics.finish: Pepper and baking spice meet dry, tannic wood.
critics.summary: An intense wheated bourbon balancing substantial fruit against assertive oak. The pictured batch is unknown, so this review supplies context rather than a transferable score.

notes: Mash bill corroborated by Breaking Bourbon; its six-year age and 121.5 proof describe October 2024 only. The photographed batch is not known.

producer.summary: Ben Holladay’s original rye-containing bourbon recipe at natural Rickhouse Proof. Kept separate from the Soft Red Wheat expression; batch strength is not fixed.

facts.age: At least 6 years; exact batch age unconfirmed

critics.nose: Sweet baking spice with cherry and toasted nuts.
critics.palate: Vanilla and caramel give way to pepper and char.
critics.finish: Long and warming, retaining spice and nutty oak.
critics.summary: A favorable review of the August 2023, 120.1-proof batch. No numeric score is assigned; the reviewer uses a buy/try/leave verdict.

notes: Recipe corroborated by the Bottled-in-Bond original review. Proof and age are not assigned from another batch.

producer.summary: The original Ben Holladay bourbon uses rye as its secondary grain, unlike Soft Red Wheat. The bonded release is bottled at 100 proof.

critics.nose: Dark caramel and leather with dry spice.
critics.palate: Full texture, oak and dark fruit.
critics.finish: Walnut and cinnamon with lingering warmth.
critics.summary: Batch 1 showed considerable spice and tannic wood alongside its substantial texture. Batch 1 is not established by the photo.

notes: Recipe and strength corroborated by the Batch 1 review. Its six-year age describes that release; no pictured batch age or numeric review score is inferred.

producer.summary: Old Grand-Dad’s bonded bourbon is at least four years old and bottled at 100 proof. Its rye-forward character pairs sweet vanilla with dried fruit and pepper.
producer.nose: Citrus peel and cinnamon over toasted wood.
producer.palate: Moderate body, vanilla and dried fruit with rye spice.

facts.region: James B. Beam Distilling Co., Kentucky

critics.nose: Cinnamon leads sweeter caramel and vanilla.
critics.palate: Concentrated spice with some dark fruit.
critics.finish: Caramel sweetness gives way to gentle oak and spice.
critics.summary: The review praises its flavor and value while noting that cinnamon dominates the profile.

producer.summary: Gunnar’s Honey blends Heritage wheated bourbon with raw Kansas honey from T-Creek Bees & Honey. It is a 70-proof honey-flavored spirit, rather than an unflavored straight bourbon.
producer.palate: Honey sweetness over a wheated-bourbon base.

facts.region: Gunnar’s, Kansas; pictured production site not established

notes: Only producer information was found. No independent critic score or tasting consensus is claimed. Natural honey can settle; the producer suggests shaking gently or chilling.

producer.nose: Vanilla, caramel and oak with a faint herbal note.
producer.palate: Smooth oak, sharp spice, honey and sweetness.
producer.summary: Extra-aged bottled-in-bond single barrel bourbon (about 40 Kentucky seasons); warm golden amber color.

critics.nose: Sweet vanilla and caramel with mature wood.
critics.palate: Oak and vanilla balanced by spice and dark sugar.
critics.finish: Moderate length with a leathery oak note.
critics.summary: A classic bourbon profile. This review is of barrel 2068; the photo does not identify a barrel, so its numeric score is not applied.

notes: The photograph confirms the ten-year bonded expression, not the barrel number. Single barrels differ; supporting review notes are not an exact-barrel score.
